entry.content:
blaze: Multiple HTTP/1.1 request-smuggling primitives in blaze's Java wire parser

Aliases: CVE-2026-73494

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.http4s:http4s-blaze-server_2.13 — fixed in 0.23.18
  • org.http4s:blaze-http_2.13 — fixed in 0.23.18
  • org.http4s:blaze-http_3 — fixed in 0.23.18
  • org.http4s:blaze-http_3 — fixed in 1.0.0-M42
  • org.http4s:blaze-http_2.13 — fixed in 1.0.0-M42

### Summary Five independent HTTP/1.1 conformance laxities in blaze's hand-written Java parser (`http/src/main/java/org/http4s/blaze/http/parser/`) cause request-boundary disagreement with a stricter intermediary. All are reachable from a default `BlazeServerBuilder` with no non-default configuration. ### Impact Actual exploitability depends on the fronting proxy — a boundary disagreement requires a *pair* of parsers that disagree. Where the proxy forwards the malformed bytes and derives a different message boundary, the consequences are the standard set: front-end ACL/auth bypass, response-queue poisoning on pooled backend connections, and cache poisoning. Risk concentrates on lenient or legacy intermediaries. ### Workarounds Deploy behind an RFC-strict reverse proxy (nginx, HAProxy…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-46q4-43ph-c6fr: blaze: Chunked-body trailer fields promoted into Request.headers in blaze-server (front-end header-sanitization bypass)
entry.content:
blaze: Chunked-body trailer fields promoted into Request.headers in blaze-server (front-end header-sanitization bypass)

Aliases: CVE-2026-73495

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.http4s:blaze-http_2.13 — fixed in 0.23.18
  • org.http4s:blaze-http_2.12 — fixed in 0.23.18
  • org.http4s:blaze-http_3 — fixed in 0.23.18
  • org.http4s:blaze-http_3 — fixed in 1.0.0-M42
  • org.http4s:blaze-http_2.13 — fixed in 1.0.0-M42

### Summary blaze-server can merge HTTP/1.1 chunked-body trailer fields into `Request.headers`. Because trailer fields are attacker-controlled, an unauthenticated remote client can inject arbitrary header names/values (e.g. `X-Forwarded-For`, internal-auth headers) that a fronting proxy sanitized from the request-header section, bypassing header-based trust decisions in the application. ### Impact Any http4s application using `BlazeServerBuilder` over HTTP/1.1 whose routes or middleware trust proxy-set headers (e.g., `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, org-internal auth headers) is affected. Where a fronting proxy strips/normalizes those headers but forwards chunked bodies with trailers intact, an attacker can spoof client IP for allow-lists/rate-limits/audit, forge …

entry.content:
blaze: Unbounded WebSocket message aggregation in http4s-blaze-server

Aliases: CVE-2026-73493

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.http4s:http4s-blaze-server_2.13 — fixed in 0.23.18
  • org.http4s:http4s-blaze-server_2.13 — fixed in 1.0.0-M42
  • org.http4s:http4s-blaze-server_2.12 — fixed in 0.23.18
  • org.http4s:http4s-blaze-server_3 — fixed in 1.0.0-M42

## Summary `http4s-blaze-server` aggregates the fragments of an incoming WebSocket message with no limit on total size or fragment count. A client that completes a WebSocket handshake can send an unterminated fragmented message and drive unbounded heap growth in the server JVM, resulting in denial of service via `OutOfMemoryError`. ## Impact Any http4s application serving WebSocket routes over `BlazeServerBuilder` is affected; no non-default configuration is required, and `maxWebSocketBufferSize` does not bound the aggregate (it bounds only individual frames). A single connection sending continuation frames that never set FIN forces the server to buffer every fragment until the heap is exhausted, terminating the JVM with `OutOfMemoryError` on the blaze selector thread. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-ghvc-7hp8-2g2v: Apache cxf-core: No restriction on attachment headers per message
entry.content:
Apache cxf-core: No restriction on attachment headers per message

Aliases: CVE-2026-50645

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.apache.cxf:cxf-core — fixed in 4.2.2
  • org.apache.cxf:cxf-core — fixed in 4.1.7
  • org.apache.cxf:cxf-core — fixed in 3.6.12

There is no restriction on the amount of attachment headers that a message can contain when being deserialized by Apache CXF, which can lead to uncontrolled resource consumption or a denial of service attack. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.2 or 4.1.7 or 3.6.12, which fix this issue by imposing a maximum default of 500 attachments per message.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-53w6-v7cv-fc9h: Spring for Apache Kafka: Improper Validation of Retry Topic Header Values Leads to Retry Sequence Manipulation
entry.content:
Spring for Apache Kafka: Improper Validation of Retry Topic Header Values Leads to Retry Sequence Manipulation

Aliases: CVE-2026-41727

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.springframework.kafka:spring-kafka — fixed in 4.0.6
  • org.springframework.kafka:spring-kafka — fixed in 3.3.16
  • org.springframework.kafka:spring-kafka
  • org.springframework.kafka:spring-kafka
  • org.springframework.kafka:spring-kafka

Spring Kafka's retry topic infrastructure did not sufficiently validate user-controlled header values before acting on them. A producer could send a record with a crafted retry_topic-attempts header to supply an out-of-range attempt count and cause the retry topic router to misidentify where the message was in the retry sequence. Affected versions: Spring for Apache Kafka 4.0.0 through 4.0.5; 3.3.0 through 3.3.15; 3.2.0 through 3.2.13; 2.9.0 through 2.9.13; 2.8.0 through 2.8.11.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-gg69-9wwp-6jx2: Spring for Apache Pulsar: JsonPulsarHeaderMapper Trusted-Package Prefix Check Allows Unintended Subpackage Deserialization
entry.content:
Spring for Apache Pulsar: JsonPulsarHeaderMapper Trusted-Package Prefix Check Allows Unintended Subpackage Deserialization

Aliases: CVE-2026-41732

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • org.springframework.pulsar:spring-pulsar — fixed in 2.0.6
  • org.springframework.pulsar:spring-pulsar — fixed in 1.2.18
  • org.springframework.pulsar:spring-pulsar

JsonPulsarHeaderMapper matched type headers against trusted packages using a prefix check, meaning that trusting any package implicitly trusted all of its subpackages. Additionally, an empty trusted-packages configuration fell back to trusting all packages rather than applying a safe default allow-list. Affected versions: Spring for Apache Pulsar 2.0.0 through 2.0.5; 1.2.0 through 1.2.17; 1.1.0 through 1.1.17.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-j388-8rm5-p97f: Spring Data REST is vulnerable to SpEL expression injection through map-typed properties when processing JSON Patch requests
entry.content:
Spring Data REST is vulnerable to SpEL expression injection through map-typed properties when processing JSON Patch requests

Aliases: CVE-2026-41729

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.springframework.data:spring-data-rest-core — fixed in 5.0.6
  • org.springframework.data:spring-data-rest-core — fixed in 4.5.12
  • org.springframework.data:spring-data-rest-core
  • org.springframework.data:spring-data-rest-core
  • org.springframework.data:spring-data-rest-core

Spring Data REST is vulnerable to SpEL expression injection through map-typed properties when processing JSON Patch (application/json-patch+json) requests. When a persistent entity exposes a Map-typed property, the JSON Pointer path segment used as the map key is embedded directly into a SpEL expression without sanitization or validation. Affected versions: Spring Data REST 3.7.0 through 3.7.19; 4.3.0 through 4.3.16; 4.4.0 through 4.4.14; 4.5.0 through 4.5.11; 5.0.0 through 5.0.5.

### Summary Netty's `DnsResolveContext` insufficiently validates the bailiwick of NS records, enabling DNS Cache Poisoning. An attacker controlling an authoritative name server for a subdomain can poison the cache for parent domains (like `.co.uk`). ### Details In `io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsResolveContext.AuthoritativeNameServerList#add` method accepts any NS record from the AUTHORITY section as long as the record's name is a suffix of the questionName. This means if the resolver queries evil.co.uk., it will accept an NS record claiming authority over co.uk.. Subsequently, the `handleWithAdditional` method caches the associated A records from the ADDITIONAL section directly into the `authoritativeDnsServerCache` under the parent domain's key (co.uk.). This bypasses standard bailiwick rule…

  • io.netty:netty-codec-haproxy — fixed in 4.1.135.Final

### Impact The HAProxy PROXY protocol v2 codec in netty leaks native or heap memory on every connection when a client sends a syntactically valid header containing nested `PP2_TYPE_SSL` TLVs (type-length-value records) at depth two or greater. The leak occurs on the successful parse path — no exception is thrown, the message fires downstream, the decoder removes itself, and the application releases the `HAProxyMessage` normally. Yet the underlying cumulation buffer (a pooled, potentially direct `ByteBuf` allocated by the channel) remains permanently pinned.

entry.content:
Netty's Lack of Lifecycle Cleanup Leads to Pooled ByteBuf Leak in RedisArrayAggregator

Aliases: CVE-2026-48006

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • io.netty:netty-codec-redis — fixed in 4.2.15.Final
  • io.netty:netty-codec-redis — fixed in 4.1.135.Final

### Impact The RedisArrayAggregator handler permanently leaks pooled direct-memory buffers when a Redis pipeline connection closes before a RESP array aggregate completes. The handler retains child messages in per-handler state (`depths` field) but defines no `channelInactive`, `handlerRemoved`, or `exceptionCaught` method to release them when the pipeline tears down. Because the leaked buffers are slices of `PooledByteBufAllocator` chunks, they prevent those chunks from being returned to the JVM-wide direct-memory pool. Repeated connection churn by any network peer monotonically drains this shared pool, eventually causing allocation failures on all Netty channels in the process.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-c2gf-v879-257j: netty-codec-http2: ByteBuf Reference-Count Leak in DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener Leads to Memory Exhaustion
entry.content:
netty-codec-http2: ByteBuf Reference-Count Leak in DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener Leads to Memory Exhaustion

Aliases: CVE-2026-48043

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • io.netty:netty-codec-http2 — fixed in 4.1.135.Final
  • io.netty:netty-codec-http2 — fixed in 4.2.15.Final

### Impact The `DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener` class orchestrates HTTP/2 decompression by embedding a per-stream `EmbeddedChannel` that runs the appropriate decompression codec (gzip, deflate, zstd) and forwards decompressed chunks to a wrapped listener. Each decompressed chunk is a pooled `ByteBuf` handed to an anonymous `ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter` tail handler, which becomes the sole owner responsible for releasing it. A remote peer could send frames that would result in the flow-controller throwing and so trigger a resource leak which at the end might take down the whole JVM due OOME.

entry.content:
Netty Vulnerable to DNS Cache Poisoning via Missing Bailiwick Checks in CNAME Records

Aliases: CVE-2026-45674

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • io.netty:netty-resolver-dns — fixed in 4.2.15.Final
  • io.netty:netty-resolver-dns — fixed in 4.1.135.Final

### Summary Netty's DnsResolveContext fails to validate the origin (bailiwick) of CNAME records in DNS responses. ### Details In `io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsResolveContext#buildAliasMap`, the resolver processes the ANSWER section of a DNS response and blindly caches all CNAME records it finds. According to https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5452#section-6 ``` Care must be taken to only accept data if it is known that the originator is authoritative for the QNAME or a parent of the QNAME. One very simple way to achieve this is to only accept data if it is part of the domain for which the query was intended. ``` ### Impact DNS Cache Poisoning (Bailiwick Bypass). Any application using Netty's DNS resolver is impacted.
